newsitem.title: UK: HeavyLift leases two Airbus freighters.
newsitem.headline: HeavyLift leases two Airbus freighters.

text.p: UK-based, Norwegian-owned HeavyLift Cargo Airlines said it has signed an agreement to lease two converted Airbus Industrie A300B4-200 freighters from U.S. company C-S Aviation Services.
It said the two former Air France passenger planes are currently being converted into freighters by British Aerospace at that company's plant near Bristol.
The first will enter service for the London Stansted airport-based all-cargo airline in August and the second in December, said a HeavyLift statement.
"The A300B4-200 makes an ideal aircraft for regional operations in Europe, the eastern Mediterranean and North Africa," said the carrier's commercial director Graham Pearce.
"Its ability to carry full-size, maindeck Boeing 747 freighter pallets also makes this a good feeder aircraft for long-haul scheduled operators," he said.
HeavyLift currently operates Belfast, Hercules and Ilyushin IL-76 freighters, along with nine 120-tonne capacity Antonov AN-124s under a joint venture with Russian all-cargo operator Volga-Dnepr.
HeavyLift is owned by Norwegian shipbuilding and engineering firm Kvaerner ASA. - Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax 5017 - www.racs.com
